en: Udāna 5.4 Kumārakasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a number of young boys were harassing some fish between Sāvatthī and Jeta’s Grove.
Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered Sāvatthī for alms.
The Blessed One saw those many boys between Sāvatthī and the Jeta Grove harassing the fish.
Having seen them, he approached where the boys were; having approached, he said this to those boys:
"Are you afraid of suffering, boys? Is suffering unpleasant to you?"
“‘Yes, venerable sir; we fear suffering, venerable sir, for suffering is unpleasant to us.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:
If suffering is unpleasant to you,
do not perform an evil deed,
If you will do, or are doing, an evil deed,
there is no escape from suffering for you.
"Even if one flees, it will still pursue.
